newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Danone takes 20 pct in Morocco dairy firm.
newsitem.headline: Danone takes 20 pct in Morocco dairy firm.

text.p: French Groupe Danone purchased 20 percent of Morocco's leading agro-industrie Centrale Laitiere capital, a statement issued by the group on Tuesday said.
Centrale Laitiere is a subsidiary of Morocco's largest private ONA Group. Both companies are listed one the Casablanca bourse and considered as a market blue chips.

"For ONA, this agreement will reinforce the technological partnership with Danone and establish the basis of development of Centrale Laitiere on the Moroccan market of fresh products," a statement sent to Reuters said.

ONA signed the agreement to cede 20 percent of its majority stake in Centrale Laitiere to Danone on September 9, 1996, the statement said. Centrale Laitiere has a turnover of 2.2 billion dirhams ($250 million), the statement added.
Danone holds already 2.74 percent of ONA Group capital under an agreement signed with the group in 1994.
The Moroccan firm holds respectively 55 percent of the market for milk and and 75 percent of market share of derivative dairy products.

"In the last decade, the company's sales grew by an average 10 percent per year, largely better than other food industry, including edible oil (+5.0 percent) and sugar (+3.0 percent)," Mohamed Mekouar, an analyst at Upline Securities, said.
